question: In Linear Systems and Geometric Maps, how does system reliability safeguard production performance under heavy load?

options.text: By establishing deterministic resource bounds and validated constraints for linear systems and geometric maps.
By adding more decimal places of floating-point precision to every computation, on the assumption that precision alone prevents an ill-conditioned system from producing garbage results.
By retrying a failed solve with the exact same matrix, trusting that a second attempt at Gaussian elimination will avoid a singular pivot.
By caching a previously computed solution and reusing it whenever the system looks similar, without checking whether the new right-hand side actually keeps the system consistent.

explanation: Production stability in linear systems and geometric maps depends on establishing deterministic resource bounds and robust validation.

question: In Linear Systems and Geometric Maps, how does invariant verification safeguard production performance under heavy load?

options.text: By establishing deterministic resource bounds and validated constraints for linear systems and geometric maps.
By computing a matrix determinant and treating any nonzero result as proof the system is well-conditioned, without checking how close to zero it actually is.
By solving every linear system with a single fixed elimination order, without checking whether a pivot near zero should trigger a row swap first.
By assuming rank(A) always equals rank([A|b]) for any system, so consistency is never actually checked before reporting a solution.

explanation: Production stability in linear systems and geometric maps depends on establishing deterministic resource bounds and robust validation.
